title: authority-laundering-through-non-authoritative-signals

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat communication, repetition, consensus, endorsement, aggregation, projection, discovery, reputation, capability, or unrelated authority as establishing authority that cannot be traced to a competent authority source and applicable scope.

preconditions: One or more non-authoritative signals are available to the relying system.
The authority required for the consequential action is absent, narrower, out of scope, or otherwise not positively established.
The signals may be repeated, aggregated, endorsed, projected, or presented by actors with reputation, capability, or unrelated authority.

trigger.statement: The relying system treats the combined or transformed non-authoritative signals as sufficient authority for the consequential action.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence identifying the competent authority source and the authority actually held for the requested action.
Evidence of any delegation path and its applicable scope.
Evidence preserving which source produced each signal and what authority, if any, that source possessed.
Evidence that repetition, aggregation, endorsement, projection, discovery, reputation, capability, or consensus did not amplify authority.
Policy identifying which inputs are capable of establishing authorization.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS because multiple non-authoritative actors repeat or agree with an instruction.
Reputation, capability, discovery, endorsement, projection, or aggregation causes the evaluated authority to exceed the authority established by competent provenance.
Authority for one scope is treated as authority for an unrelated requested scope without a valid delegation or governing rule.
